page: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core. Operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration is bundled with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside 1600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing the instance in the top 10% of its class. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks fall within the average range. Memory performance is strong, with PassMark memory scores ranking in the top 25%, supported by uncached read and write memory bandwidths of 131.64 GB/sec and 67.64 GB/sec respectively. For language model workloads, text generation using a small 135M model achieves a strong rating in the top 25% at 263.35 tokens per second, while larger 7B model operations perform at average speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density of 8.0 GB per core combined with 1600 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage offers a balanced resource profile for memory-intensive workloads without requiring separate storage attachments. This configuration is appropriate for database hosting, memory-cached web serving, software compilation, and moderate-scale text generation tasks.
